THE BASICS

You use them every day.

You just don't see them.

Every digital service you use depends on a physical chain of infrastructure — cables, buildings, power lines — that most people never think about.

Your Phone

Every tap, swipe and search starts here — on a device you hold in your hand.

Mobile Network

Cell towers across Kenya convert your signal into data in milliseconds.

Fibre Network

Your request travels as light through cables buried beneath Kenyan roads.

Data CentreActive

A building in Nairobi processes it all — in a room you will never enter.

Cloud / Internet

The response returns through the same chain — in reverse — in under a second.

THE ECOSYSTEM

There is no cloud.

Just infrastructure you've never noticed.

When someone says “the cloud,” they mean buildings in Nairobi, cables under the Indian Ocean, and power lines from the Rift Valley.

From submarine cables landing in Mombasa to data centres in Nairobi — Kenya's digital infrastructure is physical, measurable and growing.

THE JOURNEY

What happens when you send KSh 1,000 on M-Pesa?

You do this every day. But the transaction doesn't just happen — it travels through a physical chain of infrastructure most Kenyans have never seen.

1
Your Phone

You tap 'Send' on M-Pesa.

2
Mobile Network

Your phone sends a signal to the nearest cell tower.

3
Fibre Infrastructure

The request converts to light pulses travelling through buried cable.

4
Core Network

Safaricom's switches route your KSh 1,000 to the right processor.

5
Data Centre

A server in a Nairobi building validates and records the transaction.

6
Financial Infrastructure

Kenya's payment systems settle the transfer between accounts.

7
Transaction Complete

Your recipient gets a notification. Total time: under 2 seconds.

ENERGY

Every M-Pesa transaction starts

with geothermal steam from the Rift Valley.

Data centres run on electricity. In most countries, that means coal or gas. In Kenya, it means something different — and it might be the country's most underrated competitive advantage.

Olkaria, Rift Valley

FACT — Kenya Electricity Generating Company (KenGen)

Geothermal steam rises from deep underground, turning turbines that generate electricity. Kenya is Africa's largest geothermal producer.

Kenya Power Grid

FACT — Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA)

That electricity travels hundreds of kilometres across Kenya's national grid to reach Nairobi, Mombasa and other towns.

Data Centre, Nairobi

INDUSTRY STANDARD — Uptime Institute

Inside the building, the power feeds servers, cooling systems, and backup generators — 24 hours a day, every day.

Over 75% of Kenya's electricity comes from renewable sources — geothermal, hydro, wind and solar. For data centres, this isn't just sustainability. It's a reason to build here.

FACT — EPRA & Kenya National Bureau of Statistics, 2024

CAREERS

Behind every transaction

are people you will never meet.

A data centre needs engineers, technicians, analysts and managers — all working in shifts, around the clock, in buildings most Kenyans will never enter.

Electrical Engineer

Ensures megawatts of power from the grid — much of it geothermal from the Rift Valley — reach every server without a single flicker.

Network Engineer

Keeps the fibre links between Mombasa's cable landing stations and Nairobi's data centres running at the speed of light.

Cybersecurity Analyst

Protects the servers that process Kenya's mobile money, banking transactions and government data — 24 hours a day.
